title: pendingReward() view over-reports available rewards by not accounting for the _safePay balance cap
description:
`pendingReward(address)` returns `(user.amount * acc) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt` — the full theoretical entitlement — but the actual claimable amount at that instant is `min(entitlement, rewardToken.balanceOf(this))` because `_safePay` caps payout at the on-chain balance. When the pool is momentarily under-funded (e.g., between the moment accruals passed and the moment `pull()` has swept mint-debt into this contract), `pendingReward` reports a number the user cannot actually claim, and — per CS-01 — claiming still bumps their debt to the full reported value, silently forfeiting the shortfall.

Downstream UIs and keepers using this view will display inaccurate numbers and may issue `claim()` transactions that underpay without warning.
impact: User-facing display drift and, combined with CS-01, silent loss of the unpaid shortfall.
proof: Mechanical: call `pendingReward(user)` when `rewardToken.balanceOf(this) < (user.amount * acc / PREC) - user.rewardDebt`. The function returns the larger number; a subsequent `claim()` will only transfer the balance and still advance rewardDebt to the full accrual.
recommendation: Either (a) have `pendingReward` additionally clamp to `rewardToken.balanceOf(address(this))` so the UI matches what a claim would actually pay, or (b) fix CS-01 so that the unpaid shortfall rolls over and the view is accurate as a forward-looking entitlement. Preferably both: make the view clamp, and make the state-mutating path roll over.
